title: reduce streaming token latency: optimize token loop, flush cadence, backpressure, kernel scheduling
author: Noah Park
release_notes: Reduced median streaming token latency by ~18-25% for short-sequence workloads; introduces adaptive flush cadence and request-level backpressure to smooth bursts; no API changes.
body: Motivation: Streaming token latency for short sequences and bursty input patterns remains a dominant contributor to tail latency for many real-world workloads. This PR targets three sources of overhead: (1) the internal token emission loop micro-batching and scheduling jitter, (2) too-aggressive or too-conservative flush cadence that either increases per-token latency or increases syscalls and memory churn, and (3) lack of local backpressure propagation which causes head-of-line blocking when downstream is transiently slow. Summary of changes: implemented a more efficient token emission loop that avoids per-token allocation hotspots and reduces syscalls by reusing buffers; introduced an adaptive flush cadence heuristic that flushes more aggressively for long-running streams and coalesces short bursts to avoid tiny writes; added request-level backpressure tokens and a soft-priority yield path so slow connections do not block high-priority low-latency streams; added a scheduler hint path that prefers kernel-optimized dispatch for short sequence generation to reduce kernel context switches; integrated KV-cache-aware continuous batching so hot prefixes remain batched even when streaming; added metrics and tracing for flush cadence, backpressure stalls, and per-request emission latency. Implementation details: - runtime/streaming/token_loop.rs: replaced per-token Vec allocations with preallocated emission buffer and ref-counted slices; moved sequence-length checks out of the hot path; micro-batching window reduced from 8ms to adaptive 1-8ms depending on load. - runtime/streaming/flush_cadence.rs: introduced AdaptiveFlushCadence struct with simple EWMA hit-rate estimator and thresholds derived from production telemetry; uses epoch-based flush to avoid syscall storms. - runtime/scheduler/kernel_hint.rs: added KernelHint enum on request descriptor (SHORT_SEQ_OPT), scheduler uses hint to prefer a fast-path kernel selection and avoids migrating ephemeral tasks between GPU backends. - runtime/kv_cache/batching.rs: added continuous batching touchpoint so streaming requests touching the KV cache keep entries alive and participate in batching windows. - integrations/streaming_tests/*: added new synthetic and e2e tests that simulate 95th/99th percentile bursty connections and assert latency regressions are within target. Benchmarks: - Microbench (local perf harness): median per-token emission latency down 22% for short sequences (<=32 tokens) and p99 down 15%. - Staging canary (real traffic mix): end-to-end median streaming latency down 18%, p95 down 12%, no observable regression on throughput. Observability: added flush_cadence.ms histogram, backpressure.duration histogram, token_emission.count, kernel_hint.used counter, and tracing spans for emission_loop->flush. Rollout plan: staged canary across 2% -> 20% -> 100% with automatic rollback if p95 latency increases by >5% or error rate increases >1%. The initial rollout used the adaptive cadence in conservative mode; after 1 week moved to normal mode. Migration and compatibility: no API changes; token stream semantics preserved. How to revert: revert the single squashed commit or toggle the runtime config flags (streaming.adaptive_flush.enabled=false, streaming.backpressure.enabled=false). Checklist: tests added and passing, perf numbers included, docs updated with new metrics. Related: follows on work from ENG-5341 (continuous batching improvements) and complements prior PR pr-33120.
commits: Improve token emission hot path and buffer reuse
Introduce backpressure tokens and soft-priority yield
Add KernelHint short-seq fast path in scheduler
Integrate KV-cache touchpoints for continuous batching
Add telemetry for flush cadence and backpressure
review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice cleanup of the hot path, can you add a microbenchmark showing allocation counts before/after?
Noah Park: Added allocation counters in the microbench harness and linked numbers in the PR description.
Samir Patel: The EWMA thresholds look reasonable but please add a guard for cold starts where EWMA is NaN/zero.
Noah Park: Guard added (fallback to conservative cadence until 200 samples).
Riley Morgan: KernelHint feels invasive to scheduler; can we gate with config flag and measure overhead?
Noah Park: Added runtime flag scheduler.kernel_hint.enabled and added low-overhead fast-path only when enabled. Benchmarks included.
Ava Chen: Integration tests flaked once in CI on the canary test, rerun?
Noah Park: CI rerun fixed transient; added tighter timing tolerance to the test to reduce flakiness.
discussion_summary: Reviewers asked for allocation metrics, cold-start guards, and an opt-in flag for kernel hints. All items addressed. CI initially flaked on a timing-sensitive test which was hardened. Performance numbers are in the PR description and backed by microbench and staging canaries.
notes: This is a performance-focused PR; observability and runtime flags are added to assist in post-merge monitoring. No customer-visible API changes.
revert_instructions: Revert the merge commit or set streaming.adaptive_flush.enabled=false and streaming.backpressure.enabled=false via runtime config; for immediate rollback disable scheduler.kernel_hint.enabled as well.
examples: examples/streaming/streaming_perf_harness.py: small harness to reproduce perf numbers
scripts/benchmark/run_streaming_bench.sh: can run local microbench and upload results to artifacts
